section_summary: This section finishes a Tokyo despatch summarizing the Occupation’s economic and scientific work. It then contains a despatch transmitting William L. Magistretti’s reports on local government conferences in Nobeoka and Beppu, followed by duplicate copies of the despatch and reports. The reports examine local finance, schools, political parties, communism, women’s participation and the uneven progress of democratization. Page 100 begins a Yokohama covering letter for the reports.

subfiles.title: Tokyo despatch no. 902 on the Occupation’s economic and scientific work
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Summarizes an Economic and Scientific Section publication on the Occupation’s economic and scientific achievements.
subfiles.summary: The concluding pages discuss price stabilization, foreign trade and bilateral arrangements, textiles, business democratization, labor, and scientific activity. The despatch encloses eight copies of the publication.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Two Reports on Local Government Conditions in Japan
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Transmits Magistretti’s Nobeoka and Beppu reports and a Yokohama covering despatch.
subfiles.summary: Sebald forwards the reports and commends Magistretti and Finn.

subfiles.title: Local Government Conference: Nobeoka, Miyazaki Prefecture
subfiles.about: Reports on the November 7–8 local government conference and conditions in Miyazaki Prefecture.
subfiles.summary: Magistretti describes Nobeoka’s industry, politics and crop losses, then recounts conference lectures and discussion groups. Participants raised concerns about recall, neighborhood associations, conflicting tax assessments, school finance and women’s limited participation. He concludes that Miyazaki’s distance from Tokyo and limited contact with foreigners slow democratization, and questions withdrawing all Military Government teams at once.

subfiles.title: Local Government Conference at Beppu
subfiles.about: Reports on the November 10–11 conference and local political conditions in Beppu and Ōita Prefecture.
subfiles.summary: Magistretti describes Beppu’s tourism economy, Mayor Waki’s port plans and the conference proceedings. Discussion groups examined taxes, schools, civic education, political parties, communism and women’s participation; the report also records an incident involving a Nisei conference assistant. He concludes that local political bosses, communist organization and inadequate municipal funds complicate democratic reform.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Two Reports on Local Government Conditions in Japan (duplicate copy)
subfiles.from: W. J. Sebald, United States Political Adviser for Japan
subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of the despatch transmitting the Nobeoka and Beppu reports.
subfiles.summary: A library file copy repeats the transmittal and enclosure list.

subfiles.title: Local Government Conference: Nobeoka, Miyazaki Prefecture (duplicate copy)
subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of Magistretti’s Nobeoka conference report.
subfiles.summary: This copy repeats the account of Nobeoka’s economy and politics, conference discussions about recall and neighborhood associations, and concerns about taxes, schools and democratization.

subfiles.title: Local Government Conference at Beppu (duplicate copy, incomplete)
subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of the Beppu report, ending here before its concluding page.
subfiles.summary: These pages repeat the report’s account of Beppu’s economy, conference proceedings and discussions of local finance, schools, political organization, communism and women’s participation. Page 99 ends during the discussion of women and schools; the concluding page of the earlier copy does not recur in this section.

subfiles.title: Yokohama covering letter on the Kyushu local government reports
subfiles.from: Yokohama Branch, Office of the United States Political Adviser
subfiles.to: W. J. Sebald, Acting United States Political Adviser
subfiles.about: Forwards Magistretti’s two Kyushu reports and comments on local autonomy and withdrawal of Civil Affairs teams.
subfiles.summary: The letter forwards the reports, commends Magistretti and Finn, and notes local funding problems.
